newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary criticises Slovakia's import surcharge.
newsitem.headline: Hungary criticises Slovakia's import surcharge.

text.p: Hungarian Industry Minister Szabolcs Fazakas criticised Slovakia on Wednesday for introducing a seven percent import surcharge this week.

"The Slovak measure contradicts the spirit of CEFTA (Central European Free Trade Agreement)," Fazakas told the daily newspaper Nepszabadsag, adding he hoped the matter could be dissolved before the CEFTA's September summit.
Slovakia, facing serious foreign trade problems, imposed a 7.0 percent import surcharge on all goods except raw materials, effective July 21.
According to the ministry's earlier figures, Hungary's exports to Slovakia in the first five months of this year totalled $108 million, while imports from Slovakia amounted to $152 million.
